children: Gold prices fall to their lowest level in more than a year as investors weigh hawkish Federal Reserve commentary and await the release of the October meeting minutes later this week. In early European trading, New York gold futures decline 0.7% to $3,858.80 a troy ounce, extending weekly losses to more than 6% and reaching their lowest level since September 2025. Persistent inflationary pressures are raising expectations of near-term interest-rate hikes, supporting Treasury yields and raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets such as gold. Meanwhile, a stronger U.S. dollar is adding further pressure by making dollar-denominated bullion more expensive for overseas buyers. Investors are now turning their attention to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's opening remarks at the central bank's Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference on Monday, followed by the release of the October FOMC meeting minutes on Wednesday. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
